provider.notes: Registered as `openai` (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:1687); live sessions build it through create_stt_standard (gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:447). The existing client is HTTP request and response only. On a live call it buffers audio and uploads only at hang-up, when the buffer reaches 20 MB, or when the client ends its audio by hand (an audio_end message on /ws, or a buffer commit on the /v1/realtime cascade), because the default flush strategy is OnDisconnect and no configuration path sets another (gateway/src/core/stt/openai/config.rs:651; client.rs:793-823), so a normal call gets no transcript while it is in progress. Either act makes the voice manager disconnect and reconnect the client (gateway/src/handlers/ws/audio_handler.rs:301-322, also called from gateway/src/handlers/openai_realtime/cascade.rs:1353-1354; gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:1648-1672), and the disconnect uploads the buffer (client.rs:886-897). A push-to-talk client that ends each utterance itself is therefore the one kind of session that gets usable text from this provider during a call today. The same disconnect clears the result callback (client.rs:902-903) and nothing registers it again, so a second such act in the same session probably delivers nothing (inferred from reading, not run). There is no streaming speech-to-text client for OpenAI, so no native transport appears in any row. default_model is gpt-transcribe by integration decision (section 15, awaiting sign-off), while today's code still resolves an empty model to whisper-1 (config.rs:63-67, :671-674), which the vendor removes on 2027-02-26; the code default has to move to gpt-transcribe with it. There is no model allow-list: unknown ids are sent verbatim (config.rs:671-693). OpenAI, self-hosted servers, Azure OpenAI, Groq and WaaV Infer speak the same multipart request: the adapters openai_transcriptions, azure_openai_transcriptions and groq_transcriptions are one implementation with different hosts, authentication and limits. For any id outside its three-entry model list the client labels the vendor call span with a family fallback instead of the id sent (client.rs:438-444; config.rs:109-115), which matters for per-model metering. The language a session configures is mapped to ISO 639-1, with `auto` omitted, before the client is built on the /ws path (gateway/src/handlers/ws/config.rs:475-504; gateway/src/core/lang/mappers/mod.rs:218-222); the segmented adapter must take that mapped value, while the DAG node passes its own default en-US unmapped (gateway/src/dag/nodes/provider.rs:334-343). Unlike self-hosted and Azure OpenAI deployments, which are refused before a client is built (gateway/src/handlers/ws/bud_legs.rs:122-134 and, for voice-agent legs, :815-826), an `openai` session is not refused today; both sites are where an interim refusal of OpenAI file models would go.

gateway_client.notes: No adapter exists. The request and response code lives inside the buffering client: flush_buffer wraps the whole buffered call in one WAV at the session sample rate, is awaited on the audio path under the voice manager's speech-to-text write lock (gateway/src/core/voice_manager/manager.rs:636-639) and uses a 30 s timeout (client.rs:54). A stateless transcriber that takes one utterance has to be extracted from it. Field mapping must change for this model: the client sends the singular `language` field for every model (config.rs:856-858) and folds key terms into `prompt` (config.rs:773-777), while the vendor documents `languages[]` and `keywords[]` here and says not to send both language fields. The vendor call span is labelled with the model family fallback, not the id sent (client.rs:438-444), so this model is recorded as gpt-4o-transcribe. The model returns no confidence or log-probabilities; only a detected-language list, empty when not reliable. A tier 1 limit of 200,000 tokens per minute applies next to the 500 requests per minute. interim_results is post_commit because stream=true returns text deltas of an already uploaded file.

gateway_client.notes: The socket accepts only 24 kHz PCM or G.711 (mu-law or A-law), base64 inside input_audio_buffer.append, so wire audio at any other rate must be resampled. Completion events for different turns can arrive out of order and must be matched by item_id. A commit on an empty buffer is an error. The official WebSocket URL for a transcription session is unconfirmed: the gateway facade, Pipecat and LiveKit dial ?intent=transcription, while the vendor model pages name v1/realtime/transcription_sessions. For this model the socket transcribes only after input_audio_buffer.commit: audio is appended while the caller speaks and text deltas arrive after the commit. The gateway detector would send the commit at the same boundary where the file transport sends an upload.

gateway_client.notes: No adapter exists. segment_profile.rationale: Only the HTTP request timeout deviates from the gateway defaults. provenance.notes: Fail-slow default for an OpenAI model id the map has never seen: assume a file model. OpenAI has a file endpoint and the gateway has no streaming speech-to-text client for OpenAI, so a wrong guess here fails only for a realtime-only id, and it fails with the vendor naming the model. Dated snapshots of the two realtime-only models are not in the evidence; such an id lands here and should get its own row once confirmed. The client also honours an endpoint override and the OPENAI_BASE_URL environment variable (gateway/src/core/stt/openai/config.rs:28-49, :908-921), so an unknown id under this provider may be a model on an OpenAI-compatible server. File upload is the right guess for that case too, but this row sends no language hint, which costs accuracy and speed on a Whisper-family model; such a deployment should get its own row or a deployment override.
